This appeal is filed by the Insurance Company aggrieved by the award passed in MVC No.639/2010 dated 19.07.2012 on the file of the Member MACT-5, 8th Additional Judge, Court of Small Causes,
Bangalore.

8th Additional Judge, Court of Small Causes,
Bangalore
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The claim petition is filed seeking compensation of an amount of Rs.10,00,000/- for the death of the deceased in the road traffic accident.

The case of the claimant is that, on 28.09.2008 at about 5.45 am, when NC: 2023:KHC:33144 the deceased was proceeding as a pedestrian a motorcycle came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed him and due to the said impact he sustained injuries.
It is the case of the Insurance Company that, as the driver of the offending vehicle was not having valid driving license, the Insurance Company is not liable to pay the compensation.
They have relied on Exs.P6 and P7.
The Crime was registered against the driver of the offending vehicle under Section 3(1) R/w 181 of IMV Act, which clearly shows that, the driver was not having a valid and effective driving license.
The Court below had granted compensation of an amount of Rs.50,000/- and held that both the Insurance Company as well as owner of the vehicle are jointly and severally liable for the compensation.

sentences.text: 3. Learned counsel appearing for the Insurance Company submits that the Insurance company is not liable to pay the compensation as there is violation of terms and conditions of the policy.
The court below without NC: 2023:KHC:33144 considering the same has held that the Insurance Company is liable to pay the compensation.
4. Heard learned counsel for the appellant, though notice was served no vakalath is filed on the behalf of the respondents.
In this case Crime is registered and the charge-sheet is filed.

The Crime is registered under Section 3(1) R/w 181 of IMV Act along with provision of the IPC and according to the learned counsel for the appellant as per the judgment of this Court in the case of RELIANCE GENERAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED v. SHEELA DEVI AND OTHERS1, dated 30.11.2010.

entities.text: RELIANCE GENERAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED v. SHEELA DEVI AND OTHERS1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Division Bench of this Court has held that, the registration of the FIR under Section 3(1) R/w 181 of IMV Act itself is sufficient to hold that, the driver was not having valid driving license.
In this case the owner of the vehicle is not examined by the Insurance Company.

Considering the submission of the learned counsel for the appellant and the judgment of the Division Bench in the case of (2018) ACCI.C.R.249 (P & H) NC: 2023:KHC:33144 RELIANCE GENERAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED v. SHEELA DEVI AND OTHERS.

entities.text: (2018) ACCI.C.R.249 (P & H) NC: 2023:KHC:33144 RELIANCE GENERAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED v. SHEELA DEVI AND OTHERS
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Accordingly, the appeal of the Insurance Company is allowed.
i) Insurance Company shall pay the compensation amount and shall recover the same from the owner of the vehicle.
ii) Registry is directed to return the Trial Court Records to the Tribunal, along with certified copy of the order passed by this Court forthwith without any delay.
iii) The amount in deposit shall be transmitted to the Tribunal forthwith.
iv) No costs.
Pending miscellaneous petitions, if any, shall stand closed.

SD/-
